exposure: Previous CS indications (cervical dystocia, second stage arrest, failed induction with PROM)
cohort: The study included 104 women scheduled for repeat cesarean delivery.
finding: Intra-abdominal adhesions were present in 31.7% of participants, with emergency cesarean, low socioeconomic status, gestational diabetes, and certain previous CS indications significantly associated with adhesion formation, which in turn led to higher mean blood loss and longer operative time during repeat cesarean sections.
mod_finding: Emergency cesarean delivery was significantly associated with intra-abdominal adhesion formation.
